marrow__BIOCHEM_CH25_Q019.displayText:
Primase synthesizes short RNA primers that provide the 3′-OH required by DNA polymerases.

DNA primase synthesizes RNA primers during replication of DNA.
During DNA replication, DNA is synthesized using an ssDNA template. This is done by DNA
polymerases in the 5' to 3' direction. However, DNA polymerases require an RNA primer, which is
a short (10 - 200bp) double stranded region consisting of RNA paired to the DNA templete. Thus,
RNA primers serve as scaffolds to which deoxyribonucleotides are added. The RNA in the primers
is later replaced by DNA.
Other options:
Option C: Okazaki fragments are lagging strands built on RNA primers by DNA polymerase 6.
Option D: Leading strands are synthesized by DNA polymerase e. ‘ -,
emphasis: Primase synthesizes short RNA primers that provide the 3′-OH required by DNA polymerases

rationales.a: DNA polymerase extends an RNA primer with DNA; primase itself synthesizes RNA, not DNA.
rationales.c: Okazaki fragments are DNA segments made by DNA polymerase on the lagging strand, not the direct primase product.
rationales.d: The leading strand is synthesized by DNA polymerase; primase provides its initial RNA primer.

Unwinding of DNA is not a function of the DNA polymerase complex.
A number of different DNA polymerase molecules engage in DNA replication that share three
important properties: Chain elongation, processivity, and proofreading. Unwinding of DNA is
done by enzyme helicase.

rationales.a: Chain elongation is a core DNA polymerase function as nucleotides are added to the growing strand.
rationales.b: High processivity is a characteristic of replicative polymerases and their processivity factors.

marrow__BIOCHEM_CH25_Q023.takeaway: Lynch syndrome (HNPCC) is caused by mismatch-repair defects that allow replication errors to accumulate, especially in microsatellites.
marrow__BIOCHEM_CH25_Q023.displayText:
Lynch syndrome (HNPCC) is caused by mismatch-repair defects that allow replication errors to accumulate, especially in microsatellites.

Mismatch repair will be defective in a patient with multiple gastrointestinal polyps and
carcinoma, with a positive family history/history of hereditary non-polyposis colon carcinoma
(HNPCC)
Mismatch repair is a DNA repair mechanism that corrects single-nucleotide mismatches,
insertions, and deletions introduced by the DNA polymerase during DNA replication.
HNPCC or Lynch syndrome is an autosomal dominant genetic condition. It occurs due to defects
in DNA mismatch repair genes like MLH1 and MSH2. The genomes of these patients show
microsatellite instability. HNPCC is associated with a high risk of colon cancer. It may also be
associated with a risk of developing carcinomas of the endometrium, stomach, small bowel, ovary,
pancreas, and transitional cell carcinoma of the ureter and renal pelvis.
===== PDF PAGE 401 =====
The diagnostic criteria for HNPCC are referred to as the Amsterdam criteria or the 3-2-1-0 rule. It
includes:
¢ Three or more relatives with HNPCC-associated cancer (colorectal cancer, endometrial cancer,
cancer of the small bowel, ureter, or renal pelvis), one of whom is a first-degree relative of the
other two.
+ At least two successive generations affected
+ At least one case diagnosed before age 50 years
¢ Familial adenomatous polyposis excluded
¢ Tumors verified by pathologic examination.

rationales.c: Base-excision repair removes small chemically altered bases and is not the inherited pathway underlying Lynch syndrome.

marrow__BIOCHEM_CH25_Q024.takeaway: UV sensitivity, freckling and early skin cancer indicate xeroderma pigmentosum, caused by defective nucleotide-excision repair of pyrimidine dimers.
marrow__BIOCHEM_CH25_Q024.displayText:
UV sensitivity, freckling and early skin cancer indicate xeroderma pigmentosum, caused by defective nucleotide-excision repair of pyrimidine dimers.

~ to 2,
Photosensitivity, freckling and_skin‘cancer on the face in a child aare suggestive of xeroderma
pigmentosum. It is an example of defective DNA nucleotide excision repair.
In xeroderma pigmentosum, there is.an inability to repair DNA pyrimidine dimers caused by UV
exposure. It is an autoSomal recessive disease characterized by exaggerated sunburns and
pigmentary changes on exposure'to UV radiations. There is increased risk of developing
non-melanemaand melanoma skin cancers, and neurodegeneration. They are also more prone to
developing smoking-indu@ed lung cancers.
Diagnosis is mainly clinical and it can be confirmed definitively by cellular tests for defective DNA
repair. Management includes sun avoidance and regular follow-up to assess and treat any skin
cancers. There is no cure for xeroderma pigmentosum.
emphasis: UV sensitivity, freckling and early skin cancer indicate xeroderma pigmentosum, caused by defective nucleotide-excision repair of pyrimidine dimers

rationales.b: Base-excision repair handles small altered bases, not bulky UV-induced pyrimidine dimers.
rationales.c: Mismatch repair corrects replication mismatches and small insertion/deletion loops, not UV lesions.
rationales.d: Homologous repair repairs double-strand breaks using a homologous template; XP is an NER defect.

marrow__BIOCHEM_CH25_Q025.takeaway: Defective nonhomologous end joining can prevent V(D)J recombination and cause severe combined immunodeficiency.
marrow__BIOCHEM_CH25_Q025.displayText:
Defective nonhomologous end joining can prevent V(D)J recombination and cause severe combined immunodeficiency.

SCID is associated with a defective non-homologous end-joining (NHEJ).
NHEJ is a predominant pathway for DNA double-stranded break repair. NHEJ also functions in
class switch recombination, enhancing T and B cell diversity. Thus, NHEJ deficiency leads to
combined immunodeficiency due to a failure to carry out recombination efficiently.
Severe combined immunodeficiency (SCID) is characterised by defects in both
humoral and cell-mediated immune responses. Genes involved are JAK3, RAG1, and IL-7R.
Persons with SCID are extremely susceptible to recurrent, severe infections by a wide range of
===== PDF PAGE 402 =====
pathogens, including Candida albicans, Pneumocystis jirovecii, Pseudomonas species,
cytomegalovirus, varicella, and a host of other bacteria.
X-linked SCID is the most common form, accounting for 50% to 60% of cases, is X-linked, and
hence, SCID is more common in boys. The genetic defect is a mutation in the common y-chain (yc)
subunit of cytokine receptors. In these patients, the thymus contains lobules of undifferentiated
epithelial cells, resembling fetal thymus.
Autosomal recessive SCID is commonly caused by a deficiency of adenosine deaminase (ADA)
enzyme. In these patients, the thymus contains remnants of Hassall’s corpuscles.
emphasis: Defective nonhomologous end joining can prevent V(D)J recombination and cause severe combined immunodeficiency

rationales.a: Mismatch repair corrects replication errors; it is not the pathway needed to join programmed double-strand breaks during V(D)J recombination.
rationales.b: Nucleotide-excision repair removes bulky DNA adducts and UV lesions, not the double-strand breaks in V(D)J recombination.
rationales.d: Homologous recombination is another double-strand break repair pathway but is not the NHEJ defect classically associated with this SCID question.

sourceNotes: Source question/key: ED8 Biochemistry p. 387; explanation p. 401,402.

marrow__BIOCHEM_CH25_Q027.takeaway: After transplantation, donor and recipient genomes can coexist in recipient tissues; this genetic chimerism is used to monitor engraftment.
marrow__BIOCHEM_CH25_Q027.displayText:
After transplantation, donor and recipient genomes can coexist in recipient tissues; this genetic chimerism is used to monitor engraftment.

Chimeric DNA is associated with organ transplantation, especially bone-marrow transplantation.
===== PDF PAGE 403 =====
In organ transplantation, chimeric DNA refers to the mixture of donor and recipient genetic
material that occurs when donor cells begin functioning within the recipient's body. It is used for
long-term monitoring of bone marrow transplant recipients. Detecting changes in the levels of
donor-derived cells can provide early warning signs of graft failure, rejection, or relapse of
underlying disease.

emphasis: After transplantation, donor and recipient genomes can coexist in recipient tissues; this genetic chimerism is used to monitor engraftment

rationales.a: Paternity testing compares inherited alleles but does not create mixed donor-recipient DNA in one person.
rationales.b: Maternity testing likewise identifies biological relationships rather than transplant-derived chimerism.
rationales.c: Personal identification uses a person's DNA profile; the mixed donor/recipient DNA pattern is specifically associated with transplantation.

marrow__BIOCHEM_CH25_Q028.takeaway: Telomerase is an RNA-dependent DNA polymerase that extends telomeres; it maintains chromosome ends but is not itself a DNA-repair pathway.
marrow__BIOCHEM_CH25_Q028.displayText:
Telomerase is an RNA-dependent DNA polymerase that extends telomeres; it maintains chromosome ends but is not itself a DNA-repair pathway.

~~ Se.” x¢
The false statement is that telometase is involved iv DNA repair.
Telomeres are the end of chrémosomal DNA’ Since prokaryotic DNA is circular, it does not have
free ends and hence no telomeres. Thus, telomeres are present only in eukaryotes Telomeres have
TG- rich repeats and usually do not Cede for any proteins. With every DNA replication during cell
division, telomere’shortening occurs. Once telomeres are almost negligible or non-existent in
length, the DNAs unable to'replicate and the cell dies. Hence, there is a limit to the number of
times a céll’ean divide. .\°
In stem cells and cancer cells, an enzyme telomerase having reverse transcriptase activity (RNA
dependent DNA polymerase) adds telomeres to the chromosome ends, thereby preserving
chromosomal length. It allows the stem cells and cancer cells to multiply a lot more number of
times than a normal adult cell.
emphasis: Telomerase is an RNA-dependent DNA polymerase that extends telomeres; it maintains chromosome ends but is not itself a DNA-repair pathway

rationales.a: Telomerase has reverse-transcriptase activity, using its internal RNA template to extend telomeric DNA.
rationales.b: Telomerase occurs in eukaryotic cells; the statement is consistent with the source's contrast with circular prokaryotic chromosomes.
rationales.c: Telomerase counters progressive telomere shortening by adding repeat sequences; that is a central function.
